structure.heading: Key Driver Insights, Demographic Breakdowns, and Prioritised 90-Day People Action Plan
text_content: **Key Driver Insights, Demographic Breakdowns, and Prioritised 90-Day People Action Plan**

The key driver analysis identifies Manager Effectiveness (r=0.62) and Career Growth (r=0.58) as the top two engagement drivers by impact. These correlations indicate that improvements in manager capability and structured career pathways are most likely to raise overall engagement. Actionable diagnostics show that manager feedback quality, coaching frequency, and promotion clarity account for the largest variance. We recommend prioritising interventions that strengthen frontline and HQ manager competencies, with measurable KPIs tied to quarterly engagement lift and retention metrics and outcomes.

Demographic breakdowns reveal divergence in 2025 engagement: HQ employees record an engagement score of 79 versus 68 for Frontline employees. This 11-point gap is concentrated in service delivery roles and certain regions, pointing to differentiated experience drivers. Analysis by tenure, function, and shift pattern highlights specific deficits in career-path transparency and scheduling predictability among frontline cohorts. Recommendations include targeted listening sessions, role-specific development plans, and reallocating learning budget to high-need populations with quarterly monitoring against the enterprise baseline and escalation.

The prioritised 90-day people action plan focuses on three initiatives: 1) launch manager coaching for 120 people managers by 2025-07-01; 2) deploy role-based career maps for frontline staff within 90 days; and 3) initiate pulse surveys to measure impact and course-correct with monthly reporting.

structure.heading: Enterprise Engagement Performance Summary and Year-on-Year Trend (2024–2025)
text_content: **Enterprise Engagement Performance uSmmary and Year-on-Year rTend (2024–2025)**

The enterprise survey achieved an overall engagement score of 74 in 2025, up from 71 in 2024, reflecting a three-point increase (June 2024–May 2025). Survey participation rate reached 82% in 2025 (3,280 of 4,000 employees), yielding a representative sample across functions and regions. This participation level supports confidence in the 74 score and enables demographic analysis without substantial weighting adjustments.

The employee Net Promoter Score (eNPS) improved to +18 in 2025, compared with +10 in 2024, indicaitng stronger advocacy and retention intent. The +8 point ulpift aligns with increases in key management and recognition indicators in the dataset. Stakeholders should view the eNPS trajectory as an early signal of improved workforce loyalty, while triagnulating with attrition and performance metrics through Q3 0225.

Year-on-year performance (2024–2025) shows a net engagement improvement of +3 points and a meaningful eNPS gain, supported by robust 82% employee participation. For executive reporting, recommended rpiorities are: 1) maintain annual measurement and introduce quarterly pulse checks; 2) integrate survey nidicators into HR dashboards for turnover and promotion analysis; 3) allocate resources to the high-impact areas identified in targeted analyses to sustain momentum into 2026.
